Let
\[
f(z)=(-1)^{q(z)},\qquad z\in V.
\]
Since \(f(0)=1\), we have \(q(0)=0\). The four-point identity says exactly that \(q\) is a quadratic refinement of \(\omega\):
\[
q(z+r+s)+q(z+r)+q(z+s)+q(z)=\omega(r,s).
\]
Thus every such \(q\) is
\[
q=q_0+\ell,\qquad q_0(x,y)=x\cdot y,
\]
where \(\ell\) is linear on \(V\).

The operator \(A\) is convolution by \(H\). Since \(H=-H\), \(A\) is self-adjoint. Also \(H=C\cup 63C\), where
\[
C=\{1,2,4,8,16,32,64\}.
\]
For a primitive \(127\)-th root \(\alpha\in\mathbb F_{128}\), the eigenvalues of \(A\) are
\[
\eta_j=\sum_{h\in H}\alpha^{jh}
=\operatorname{Tr}(\alpha^j)+\operatorname{Tr}(\alpha^{63j})\in\mathbb F_2.
\]
Checking the nine \(H\)-cosets gives
\[
\eta_j=0\quad\text{for }j=9,11,19,21,
\]
and \(\eta_j=1\) for the other five cosets. Also \(\eta_0=|H|=14=0\). Hence
\[
\dim\ker A=1+4\cdot 14=57.
\]
Because the eigenvalues are only \(0,1\), we have \(A^2=A\).

Now
\[
S(x,y)=(x+Ay,\;Ax+(I+A)y).
\]
Using \(A^2=A\), one checks
\[
q_0(S(x,y))=q_0(x,y),
\]
and \(S\) is symplectic. Therefore the \(S\)-invariant quadratic refinements are precisely
\[
q=q_0+\omega(a,\cdot)
\]
with \(Sa=a\). The fixed space satisfies
\[
Sa=a
\iff Ay=0,\quad A(x+y)=0.
\]
So, writing \(K=\ker A\),
\[
\operatorname{Fix}(S)=\{(p+y,y):p,y\in K\},
\]
and therefore
\[
|\operatorname{Fix}(S)|=2^{114}.
\]

For a quadratic refinement \(q\), its normalized Walsh transform has the form
\[
\mathcal F((-1)^q)(w)=\sigma(q)(-1)^{q(w)},
\]
where \(\sigma(q)=\pm1\). The condition \(Tf=f\) forces both \(q(Sz)=q(z)\) and \(\sigma(q)=1\).

For \(q=q_0+\omega(a,\cdot)\),
\[
\sigma(q)=(-1)^{q_0(a)}.
\]
Thus we must count fixed \(a=(p+y,y)\) with
\[
q_0(a)=(p+y)\cdot y=p\cdot y+y\cdot y=0.
\]
The dot product restricted to \(K\) is nondegenerate, since \(A\) is self-adjoint idempotent. For \(y=0\), all \(2^{57}\) choices of \(p\) work. For each nonzero \(y\in K\), exactly half of the \(p\in K\) work. Hence the count is
\[
2^{57}+(2^{57}-1)2^{56}
=2^{113}+2^{56}.
\]

\[
\boxed{2^{113}+2^{56}}
\]
